title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure in an automated licence plate reader, and it propagated into a physical arrest. The camera matched a plate to a vehicle of the wrong make and body type, a Chevy Malibu against a red Dodge Ram pickup, and the officers who stopped the driver were acting on that match as though it were a confirmed hit. The error was not caught before the stop, and it was only corrected afterwards, when officers learned the plate had not been stolen.

The failure sits at the handoff between an automated alert and a human decision to act on it. Nothing in the reporting shows a step that would have compared the flagged plate against the vehicle in front of the officers, or that would have required confirmation from a second source before a stop escalated. A mismatch between the flagged vehicle and the observed one is the kind of discrepancy a verification step is meant to surface, and here it went unremarked until after the arrest.

What is not established is what the camera's error rate is, whether this misread was known beforehand, or what discipline or further action may follow for the officers under investigation. The department's own K-9 policy sets out factors handlers should weigh before deploying a dog, and the reporting does not say how those factors were applied. An internal investigation finding no wrongdoing is a finding by the department, not an adjudication of the underlying stop.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police released body camera video showing officers drawing guns and using a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. The stop happened after a FLOCK camera wrongly flagged a stolen plate. The camera image matched a Chevy Malibu, but the plate was actually on a red Dodge Ram pickup. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, got out with his hands up, then walked onto the grass. He was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction. Officers later learned the plate was not stolen and that the camera had misread it. Upchurch received medical attention at the scene.

Multiple Toledo Police officers are under investigation over the incident. Police said they believed the driver might flee and did not know if he or a passenger had weapons. The department's K-9 policy says handlers should weigh the crime's severity, any immediate threat, and whether a suspect is resisting or trying to evade arrest before deploying a dog. The article does not say what discipline or further action may follow.
